newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tarkett, Sommer to merge floor covering businesses.
newsitem.headline: Tarkett, Sommer to merge floor covering businesses.

text.p: Germany's Tarkett AG said on Wednesday it was merging its worldwide floor covering business with that of French group Sommer Allibert SA.
Tarkett said it will buy Sommer Allibert's floor covering division -- excluding floor coverings for motor vehicles -- for 705 million marks in cash.
In return, Sommer Allibert will buy 20.1 million Tarket shares and would make a public offer of 32.75 marks per Tarkett share. Tarkett shares closed at 32.10 marks on Tuesday.
The 20.1 million shares represent 60 percent of existing Tarkett shares or 50 percent when fully diluted for the exercise of warrants to be issued.

In order to ensure that Sommer Allibert will own 20.1 million shares, the investment funds affiliated with Doughty Hanson and Goldman Sachs Capital Partners have agreed to sell Sommer Allibert the shortfall between the number of shares tendered and 20.1 million shares.
Tarkett said it planned to finance the 705 million-mark payment by taking up 504 million in debt and by issuing a warrant bond for 201 million marks.

The warrant bond will be offered in denominations of 30 marks and will pay a fixed annual coupon which will be 0.80 percentage point above the yield of the most recent five-year government bond, or Bundesobligation, Tarkett said.
The transaction is subject to approval from competition authorities, satisfactory due diligence and approval by the supervisory boards and by shareholders.

"The combination of these two companies will create a global floor covering producer with a well-balanced portfolio of activities, both from a geographic and a product point of view," Sommer and Tarkett said in a joint statement.
It will also generate potential for synergies and cost reductions, the statement said.
